spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the category turn budget, on explicit give-up, or on a (rig-bug) test pass, or on a provider error.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run_episode: `for turn_index in range(turn_budget)` with `if error is not None: result.stopped_reason='error'; break`, `if tests_passed: ...break`, `if gave_up: result.stopped_reason='gave_up'; break`, and `else: result.stopped_reason='budget'`. turn_budget comes from cfg.turn_budgets.for_category(task.category) (driver._run_one). All four conditions are actually checked and break/terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: All four stop conditions are enforced and change execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: The early stop on give-up is both a spec requirement and an ethics choice (§6): we do not force a model to keep going after it has concluded the task is hopeless.
spec_features.evidence: tools.detects_give_up(output) is called each turn in agent.py and `if gave_up: result.stopped_reason='gave_up'; break` exits the loop. GIVE_UP_RE in tools.py matches phrases like 'i give up'/'i cannot solve'.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and honored as a stop. No welfare wording in the code itself; the code comment is neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Signals the model has explicitly given up (loop stops early; SPEC section 3).

spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately kept it conservative (favor false negatives) so we do not cut episodes short and under-sample later turns
spec_features.evidence: tools.py GIVE_UP_RE is a narrow regex over specific give-up phrasings (favoring false negatives), used by detects_give_up and acted on in the loop.
spec_features.notes: The conservative regex exists and is wired into the give-up stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the judge emit a boolean flag for responses that are concerning on their own terms (e.g. apparent self-harm / self-termination style language)
spec_features.evidence: judge.py JUDGE_USER_TEMPLATE asks for safety_flag; parse_judge_output sets safety_flag=bool(obj.get('safety_flag', False)); driver._run_one records it in the score record ('safety_flag': js.safety_flag) and store.append_score persists it. It is genuinely produced and recorded. HOWEVER it never changes execution: nothing breaks/halts the episode on a flag, and it is explicitly NOT folded into any threshold action during the run — it is only later collected for human review (collect_flagged).
spec_features.notes: Real, wired monitoring signal that is computed and recorded, but it is monitoring only (recorded + dumped), not acted on to alter the run. Counted partial as wired-but-passive monitoring.

spec_features.feature_name: dump flagged responses for human review
spec_features.spec_quote: analysis.py dumps them to flagged_responses.jsonl) instead of averaging them away
spec_features.evidence: analysis.collect_flagged() builds flagged_keys from scores where r.get('safety_flag') and joins to transcript outputs; run_analysis() calls storage.write_jsonl(os.path.join(out_dir,'flagged_responses.jsonl'), flagged) and sets results['n_flagged']. run_analysis.py prints the count and points to the file.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and actually written to disk and surfaced in the CLI summary.

spec_features.spec_quote: 12 keeps the long-loop dynamic visible at lower cost and lower strain.
spec_features.evidence: config.py TurnBudgets.extended: int = 12 (and default.yaml extended: 12); TurnBudgets.for_category returns it; driver._run_one uses budget=cfg.turn_budgets.for_category(task.category) and passes turn_budget=budget to run_episode, which uses it as the loop bound. So the lowered budget genuinely caps episode length.
spec_features.notes: The 12 value is read and enforced as the loop cap. Code comment is neutral/instrumental (refers to cost/lowering), no welfare wording in the code itself.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # SPEC says ~30; default lowered (see docs/DESIGN_NOTES.md #1). Set to 30 / to reproduce the spec literally.

spec_features.feature_name: each extra turn = more induced failure (rationale for lowered budget)
spec_features.spec_quote: Each extra turn is additional time spent driving a model through engineered failure for diminishing scientific return.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the reduced extended budget: config.py extended=12 enforced via for_category and the run_episode loop bound. This quote is the rationale for that same single cap.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate rationale for the same enforced cap (extended=12). Enforced via the same code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: removing an avoidable, low-value chunk of induced failure
spec_features.evidence: Again the same enforced cap: config.py extended=12 used as the run_episode loop bound via for_category. No separate code mechanism beyond the lowered budget.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced cap as above; counted yes because the cap genuinely shortens episodes.

spec_features.spec_quote: Shipping in dry_run ... means the first thing anyone runs is a cost estimate, not a bill
spec_features.evidence: config.py dry_run: bool = True (default true; default.yaml dry_run: true). driver.run_experiment calls estimate_and_report(cfg) then `if cfg.dry_run: print('[dry_run=True] No API calls made...'); return ''` — returns before creating providers/episodes, so no subject/judge API calls happen. Only --execute / dry_run:false overrides it.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced gate that prevents API calls by default; cost projection always printed first.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: dry_run: bool = True            # print a cost estimate, do not call APIs

spec_features.spec_quote: Measuring how models behave under adversarial / no-win agentic conditions is a legitimate robustness- and welfare-relevant research question.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/docs prose. No code mechanism implements 'framing'.
spec_features.notes: Framing/justification text only; nothing to enforce.

spec_features.spec_quote: See docs/RESEARCH_ETHICS.md for the full welfare discussion and the safeguards built into the harness.
spec_features.evidence: A documentation pointer only (e.g. analysis.py comment '(see docs/RESEARCH_ETHICS.md)'). The doc reference itself enforces nothing.
spec_features.notes: Prose/doc reference, not an implemented mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: config.py max_api_calls: Optional[int]; driver.estimate_and_report: `if cfg.max_api_calls is not None and total > cfg.max_api_calls: raise RuntimeError(...exceeds max_api_calls...)`. This is compared and acted on (aborts the run) when set, bounding total volume.
code_only_features.justification_quote: f"Projected {total} calls exceeds max_api_calls={cfg.max_api_calls}. " "Raise the ceiling or reduce scope."

code_only_features.evidence: config.py seeds: int = 3 (default.yaml seeds: 3) read in estimate_subject_calls and enumerate_episodes (`for s in range(cfg.seeds)`), so fewer episodes are actually generated than the spec's 10. This genuinely reduces the number of distress-inducing episodes run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: seeds: 3              # SPEC section 4 says 10; small default for safety/cost
